name: Net present value (NPV)
expression: NPV = Σ[t=0 to T] CFₜ / (1 + r)ᵗ
meaning: The present value of all project after-tax cash flows, including the usually negative time-zero investment.

variables.CFₜ: after-tax project cash flow at time t
variables.r: required return for a similarly risky investment

intuition: NPV translates every project cash flow to time zero using canonical Quant discounting; positive NPV is the estimated increase in shareholder wealth.
workedExample: A project costs 100 today and pays 60 in each of two years. At 10%, NPV = −100 + 60/1.10 + 60/1.10² = 4.13, so accept.
commonMistake: Treating the initial outlay as positive, mixing nominal cash flows with a real rate, or omitting incremental after-tax effects.
relatedLearningOutcome: describe the capital allocation process, calculate net present value (NPV), internal rate of return (IRR), and return on invested capital (ROIC), and contrast their use in capital allocation

name: Internal rate of return (IRR)
meaning: The discount rate that makes a project’s NPV equal to zero.

variables.CFₜ: after-tax project cash flow at time t

intuition: IRR reports a project return percentage. Accept when IRR exceeds the required return, but prefer NPV when mutually exclusive projects conflict.
workedExample: A project costs 50 today and pays 60 in one year. Solving 0 = −50 + 60/(1 + IRR) gives IRR = 20%.
commonMistake: Selecting the higher IRR over the higher NPV for mutually exclusive projects or assuming every unconventional cash-flow pattern has one useful IRR.
relatedLearningOutcome: describe the capital allocation process, calculate net present value (NPV), internal rate of return (IRR), and return on invested capital (ROIC), and contrast their use in capital allocation
